summary: MATERIAL SATURDAY UPDATE: Pittsburgh officially downgraded WR Michael Pittman Jr. to OUT at 13:31 ET, superseding the prior archive's stale statement that no new Saturday designation changed PIT@NE. Pittman played 59 offensive snaps (about 88%) and led Pittsburgh with 58 receiving yards in Week 1, so his absence materially changes the Steelers target tree. A new Aaron Rodgers Under 0.5 interceptions candidate also surfaced after the Pittman update. Action Network published a 16:01 ET book-specific snapshot of U0.5 at bet365 -135, DraftKings -139 and Caesars -141, with its model at 0.44 interceptions / 35.7% chance of at least one interception. Independent current public pages around this run show U0.5 -139, corroborating that the market remains near the Action snapshot, but they do not identify a current executable sportsbook. PRIME therefore treats this as a conditional BET requiring a live-app price check rather than falsely asserting that a named book still has the earlier quote. Internal fair Under probability is conservatively haircutted to 63.0% because Pittsburgh threw 40 times in Week 1 and Pittman's absence creates receiver-quality uncertainty. Play only U0.5 at -143 or better, 0.5u; do not chase to Action's looser -150 ceiling. Pat Freiermuth and DK Metcalf receive target-vacuum WATCH upgrades but are not formal bets because current book-specific prices and fair distributions are not strong enough. Rico Dowdle O8.5 attempts remains directionally supported by Pittman's absence but the stored 8.5/-115 price ceiling still controls; no stake increase. Existing Josh Downs and Dalton Schultz states are unchanged. No new Grok pass and no confirmed Week 2 straight ticket in bet_history.

decisions.reason: Rodgers threw only seven interceptions in 16 games in 2025 and none on 40 attempts in Week 1. Action's quantified model projects 0.44 interceptions and a 35.7% chance of at least one. New England produced 10 interceptions in 2025 and none in Week 1. PRIME haircuts Action's 64.3% Under probability to 63.0% for pass-volume and Pittman-out uncertainty. At -139 the raw edge is about 4.84 percentage points; -143 is the maximum price that preserves roughly a 4-point edge. Exact named-book prices from 16:01 ET must be rechecked in the live sportsbook before placement; current public -139 corroboration is not treated as sportsbook-specific executable truth.

Pittman OUT is mildly supportive of run volume but does not erase the committee or negative-script risk with Pittsburgh an underdog. Do not increase the 59% fair probability or stake without stronger evidence. Prior exact 8.5/-113 market was not reverified after the Pittman news in this pass; preserve the 8.5/-115 hard ceiling.

Pittman vacates an 88% Week 1 snap role and 58 receiving yards. Freiermuth had 70.3% snaps, 72.1% route share, 12.2% target share, five catches for 46 yards and two red-zone targets, but only an 8.7% first-read share. Current public price references are inconsistent and no exact book-specific edge is verified; WATCH only.

Metcalf already had a workhorse Week 1 role (roughly 96% snaps, 10 official targets / 11 true targets). Pittman OUT raises target concentration potential, but expected Christian Gonzalez shadow coverage and a public receiving-yards market around the mid-50s prevent a quantified BET without a stronger fair-line edge.
